geo.label: on hold / minutes and PCE ahead
parts: Macro Stance

With no new US data, the debate shifts to the Fed: the dollar held gains in thin trading as markets await the Fed minutes and US GDP [[n6731]], with PCE also due [[n6703]]. Traders still put 50% odds on three cuts this year [[n6495]]. Mixed — the macro supports patience, but the S&P 500 is once again unable to surmount the 7,000 threshold [[n6716]].
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.40% and the 10Y at 4.04%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +64 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 16 bps and the 10Y 13 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13). The curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, after a bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more). The S&P 500 last closed at 6,836.17, down 1.56% over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 20.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
New / Most Important

Two policy shifts matter more than the holiday tape. The Fed is set to loosen bank rules to boost mortgage lending [[n6686]] — easier housing credit without a rate cut — and ABN AMRO frames the Warsh agenda as a 'reverse Operation Twist' [[n6706]], a balance-sheet mix that would lift the long end relative to the front.
Playbook ✓

Keep the 5Y long at 3.61% and add a 2s10s steepener from +64 bps, which wins under both a cut and a Warsh balance-sheet shift (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13). Stay underweight the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ down 3.19% over 20 sessions) until big tech stabilises (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Change the call if the minutes rule out cuts before mid-year and the 2Y retakes 3.56% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13).

geo.label: ECB on hold / rotation continues
parts: Macro Stance

Europe opened the week firmer: the STOXX 600 edged higher on financial gains ahead of key earnings [[n2279]]. The fundamentals behind the rotation have not changed — January inflation fell to 1.7% [[n2073]] — and a fund manager pivoting from the US toward Europe captures the flow argument [[n2285]].
Activity & Inflation

The STOXX 600 closed at 618.52, up 0.13% and 1.89% over 20 sessions; the FTSE 100 and CAC 40 are up 2.73% and 2.52% over 20 sessions while the DAX is down 0.63% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). EUR/USD held at 1.1867, up 2.09% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16) — a currency tailwind that keeps imported inflation low and the ECB on hold.
New / Most Important

Two frictions surfaced. Reuters notes Europe's earnings are gaining pace while lofty valuations cap the rewards [[n2281]], so beats now earn less. And luxury stocks' volatility highlights AI jitters and hedge fund positioning [[n2282]] — the sector most owned by foreigners is also the most crowded.
Playbook ✓

Stay overweight European banks and value-tilted markets (FTSE 100, CAC 40) against US growth; underweight luxury and German exporters. Change the view if valuation caps turn into outright sell-on-beat reactions in the banks, or if the euro's 20-session gain reverses.

geo.label: holiday lull / AI-plus push
parts: Macro Stance

With the mainland market shut for the Lunar New Year [[n0862]], the signal comes from Beijing's agenda and from Hong Kong. Xi prioritises 'AI-plus' and consumer spending to counter economic risks [[n0840]] — a policy mix that supports tech and services rather than property or heavy industry. We stay Mixed: the growth engines being promoted are real, but the old ones are still shrinking.
PMIs & Activity

The latest official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in January [[n0481]], and January car sales fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years [[n0601]]. No new activity print arrives during the holiday; the February PMIs need to put the official index back above 50 before the services-led stabilisation story can be trusted.
Credit Impulse

January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists [[n0723]]. The constraint is demand, not supply: banks have liquidity, households lack the confidence to borrow against falling home prices. Until household lending turns positive in a sustained way, the credit impulse feeds asset prices — which is why Hong Kong equities can rally while loan growth disappoints.
Property

A Hong Kong court dismissed the 2024 petition to wind up Country Garden [[n0849]], which removes a liquidation overhang and lets the restructuring proceed. It does not change demand: new home prices extended their decline in January [[n5950]]. Treat developer-credit relief as a tail-risk reduction for banks and bondholders, not as a housing recovery signal.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The plan to invest 5 trillion yuan in the power grid over five years [[n0578]] remains the clearest fiscal line, and it fits Xi's 'AI-plus' framing because data centres need grid capacity. On trade, Reuters reported Trump paused China tech bans ahead of a Xi summit [[n0695]]; the truce holds as long as the summit stays on track.
Markets & Flows

The Hang Seng closed at 26,705.94, up 0.52% and 0.53% over 20 sessions, while the Shanghai Composite's last print is 4,082.07 from before the holiday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16; Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). USD/CNY ticked up 0.11% to 6.9080 but is down 0.86% over 20 sessions; ASHR last closed at 33.68 and KWEB at 32.79, down 9.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16; Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Hong Kong stocks wrapped up their best lunar-year performance in eight years [[n0856]].
New / Most Important

Foreign money is coming back to Asia: hedge funds bought the most Asian stocks in a decade, Goldman says [[n2579]]. In China, Beijing's 'AI-plus' priority gives that bid a natural home in tech. The risk is that flows are running ahead of earnings — a theme the divergence below makes explicit.
Playbook ✓

Own Hong Kong-listed AI and tech leaders and grid-equipment suppliers; stay out of developers and platform names still fighting price wars. Keep a modest long-CNY bias while USD/CNY trends lower. Upgrade to Bullish if the first post-holiday credit data show household borrowing turning up; downgrade if the tech-ban pause is reversed. ⚠ Divergence: Bloomberg reports China's stock bull run is faltering with earnings set to underwhelm [[n6039]] — flows are ahead of profits.

geo.label: April hike in view
parts: Macro Stance

Japan's Q4 GDP grew an annualized 0.2%, below expectations [[n3116]]. Yet the policy read is hawkish: Ueda said Takaichi made no specific request at their meeting [[n3106]], and a former board member sees an April hike as likely [[n3105]]. A central bank left free to normalise into weak growth is the bullish signal for the yen, if not for exporters.
Activity & Currency

The Nikkei 225 closed at 56,806.41, down 0.24%, as rising BOJ hike odds weighed [[n3114]], but it is still up 5.32% over 20 sessions; USD/JPY ended little changed at 152.78, down 3.02% over 20 sessions and 2.84% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). Reuters reported the yen dipping after the soft growth figures [[n3108]] — a pause, not a reversal.
Playbook ✓

Own the yen against the dollar and Japanese banks over exporters into a spring hike. Reverse if a weak first-quarter run-up prompts the government to lean on the BOJ after all, or if USD/JPY reclaims 157.5, its level 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16).

geo.label: one-and-done? / equities over AUD
parts: Macro Stance

The RBA's latest communication cooled the hawkish story: the bank sees no set path for future rates after its February hike [[n0272]], and top forecasters say the RBA may well be done [[n0275]]. A hike that looks like one-and-done is good news for equities and less so for the currency.
Demand & Financing

The ASX 200 rose 0.55% to 8,966.80, while AUD/USD slipped 0.24% to 0.7070, still up 5.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). Corporate confidence is visible in M&A — the A$11.7 billion Macquarie-Qube deal [[n0276]] — and in results: BHP beat as copper overtook iron ore in earnings on AI-driven demand [[n5186]].
Playbook ✓

Shift from long AUD to ASX equities: copper-heavy miners and banks with deposit franchises. Take profits on the currency leg while the RBA sounds done. Change the call if monthly CPI re-accelerates and the 'no set path' language turns into another hike signal.

geo.label: March cut in play / fiscal watch
parts: Monetary & Activity

GDP growth accelerated to 4% in Q4 (PKB przyspieszył do 4 procent) [[n3536]], and January CPI came in on target but above forecasts, with experts weighing the odds of a March cut (Inflacja w celu, ale powyżej prognoz) [[n3629]]. Bankier writes that inflation surprised 'but the MPC won't let up' and that 'the decision is already settled' (RPP nie odpuści. Decyzja jest już przesądzona) [[n3725]].
FX & Markets

USD/PLN closed at 3.5464, down 2.33% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.2084, down 0.31%; the WIG20TR tracker rose 0.15% to 66.90 and is up 3.0% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). EPOL last closed at 37.67, up 4.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) — currency and equities are rising together, the sign of foreign inflows rather than local speculation.
Companies

KGHM fell 3.91% after a Citi analyst cut the recommendation (Analityk Citi ściął rekomendację dla akcji KGHM) [[n3760]]. Orlen announced a strategy update with hundreds of billions in planned investment (Setki miliardów na inwestycje) [[n3747]]; it is up 11.37% and PGE 11.95% over 20 sessions, while Pekao rose 0.95% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16).
Security & New Development

The state budget posted a deficit of 3.7 billion zlotys at the end of January, PAP reports [[n3236]]. Defence is the swing factor: the minister told arms sellers that access to Polish orders requires investing locally [[n3235]], which supports domestic suppliers but adds to the bill.
Playbook ✓

Own Polish duration and the zloty against the dollar into a likely March cut; in equities prefer Orlen and PGE on momentum and the banks over KGHM until its downgrade cycle settles. Change the call if February CPI moves back above target. ⚠ Divergence: the budget deficit is widening while bond yields sit near two-year lows — the market is pricing the easing cycle, not the fiscal trajectory.
Narrative

XLK last closed at 139.56, down 4.06% over 20 sessions, with Microsoft down 12.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Reuters tallies big tech stocks losing billions as AI spending fears hit valuations [[n6711]] — the market now doubts both the spenders' returns and the software that AI may replace.
Reported

The reporting window's message stands: Cisco fell 7% on a mediocre forecast even as earnings and revenue topped estimates [[n1770]]. No fresh US results arrived over the long weekend to change that verdict.
EPS Upside Watch

Hardware with pricing power — memory, storage and networking — is where estimates rise. Apple, down 8.03% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), is the test of whether brand power covers memory costs.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Even the winners are turning sceptical: a fund beating 99% of peers sees few software firms surviving AI [[n5083]]. When top performers capitulate on a group, positioning is usually close to washed out — watch for the first software beat that is rewarded.
Narrative

XLC last closed at 114.58, down 1.40% over 20 sessions, with Meta up 3.06% and Alphabet down 8.13% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The Times argues Alphabet's century bond raises the spectre of Motorola's fall [[n2569]] — the bear case that 100-year debt can mark peaks in corporate confidence.
Reported

Pinterest sank nearly 17% as tariffs hit earnings [[n1980]], the clearest ad-market casualty of the window. Netflix last closed at 76.87, down 12.70% over 20 sessions, and Disney at 105.45 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
EPS Upside Watch

Content owners: ByteDance committed to change after a legal threat from Disney [[n0855]], a sign that IP holders retain leverage over the largest platforms. That supports licensing upside for studios with deep libraries.
⚡ Breaking Convention

In an AI scare, owning content is turning into a defensive moat rather than a legacy liability. ByteDance's concession to Disney and Netflix's de-rating make old-media names the contrarian long inside XLC, against debt-funded platform capex.
Narrative

XLF last closed at 51.65, down 5.00% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), after the AI scare hit banks and brokers. Two new signals cut the other way: the Fed is set to loosen bank rules to boost mortgage lending [[n6686]], and European financials led the STOXX 600 higher [[n2279]].
Reported

European banks delivered the beats in the window — NatWest posted a 24% surge in annual profits [[n1931]] — and the regulatory turn in the US adds capital capacity before any rate cut. Bank of America is down 7.04% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), so the group starts from oversold.
EPS Upside Watch

Mortgage-heavy lenders and regional banks benefit most from looser rules and lower long yields. Alternative managers are the opposite trade: their private-credit books carry the software exposure the AI scare is repricing.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The FT's headline — bank CEOs party like it's 2007 [[n5104]] — is the warning. Deregulation plus exuberance at the top is a late-cycle signal; own the banks for the deregulation trade, but keep private-credit and BDC exposure underweight.
Narrative

XLE last closed at 54.35, up 14.16% over 20 sessions, and Brent at 67.75 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Oil rose on the US-Iran talks as Asian markets made a cautious start [[n6705]] — the geopolitical premium is still being added, not removed.
Reported

TotalEnergies halved buybacks while keeping its growth plans as low oil and gas prices weigh on profits [[n1817]]. European majors are rebuilding balance sheets, so the rotation favours majors that have not had to cut payouts.
EPS Upside Watch
Crude-weighted US producers carry the upside if the Iran premium holds; gas-weighted names do not, with Henry Hub at 3.24 and down 5.23% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
⚡ Breaking Convention

European gas prices are sliding as mild weather tempers supply fears [[n5099]] — the energy complex is splitting, with oil carrying a war premium and gas pricing a glut. Own oil-levered equities as a geopolitical hedge, avoid gas producers.
Narrative

XLI last closed at 174.17, up 5.06% over 20 sessions, with Caterpillar up 19.63% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The new driver is defence: Europe aims to rely less on US defence after Trump's Greenland push [[n2832]], which means multi-year procurement for European and US suppliers alike.
Reported
FedEx said an 'exceptional' holiday season will drive an expected third-quarter beat [[n1847]] — the freight cycle is firmer than the AI-disruption scare in trucking implies.
EPS Upside Watch

Power equipment for data centres and grids: utility plans such as Duke's $103B programme [[n1920]] feed turbine, engine and switchgear order books, which is where industrial estimate revisions should come from next.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Europe's defence push is a demand shock for its own industry first; US primes may face 'buy European' preferences. Favour European and dual-listed defence suppliers over US primes within the same theme.
Narrative

XLY last closed at 116.18, down 5.31% over 20 sessions, with Amazon down 16.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The low end of the consumer is trading up and down at once: Dollar Tree is quietly adding more higher-priced items [[n2589]].
Reported
Uber dropped 6.4% over the week after an earnings miss and robotaxi expansion [[n1983]] — growth platforms are being priced on margin risk, not on volume.
EPS Upside Watch
Home-improvement and repair (Home Depot up 3.14% over 20 sessions) benefits from lower mortgage rates without needing housing turnover (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Discounters chasing richer shoppers is a sign that middle-income spending is migrating down-market — good for value retail, bad for mid-priced discretionary brands. That keeps XLY a two-way sector, and its megacap weights keep it net negative.
Narrative

XLP last closed at 89.51, up 8.67% over 20 sessions, with Walmart up 12.32% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Walmart's results and fresh economic data lead the week ahead [[n0305]], so staples' leadership faces its first real test.
Reported
Coca-Cola forecast modest growth amid demand concerns [[n1697]] — the brand-owners are guiding cautiously, and the sector's gains are about safety, not acceleration.
EPS Upside Watch

Scale grocers win if trading-down continues; but retailers and shoppers are confused by new SNAP food restrictions [[n5156]], a near-term friction for low-income basket sizes that Walmart's guidance must address.
⚡ Breaking Convention

An 8.67% 20-session gain for a sector guiding to modest growth is a valuation move (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). If Walmart beats and still falls, the defensive rotation has run its course — keep the overweight with tight stops.
Narrative

XLV last closed at 157.67, up 0.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The obesity split continues — Lilly blew past estimates [[n1370]] while Novo sank 17% on a bleak 2026 forecast [[n1378]] — and generic competition is arriving abroad.
Reported
Natco Pharma shares rose more than 11% after the firm received approval to launch semaglutide in India [[n5166]] — a visible crack in GLP-1 pricing outside the US.
EPS Upside Watch
UnitedHealth sits 13.50% lower over 20 sessions after a 3.10% bounce (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13): managed care carries low expectations, the precondition for positive surprises.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Generic semaglutide in large markets compresses the global price umbrella for branded GLP-1s over time — a slow headwind for Novo first and Lilly later, and a bigger one for cash-pay compounders.
Narrative

XLB last closed at 53.31, up 8.88% over 20 sessions, with gold at 5,046.30 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). BHP's results crystallised the copper thesis: profit beat forecasts as copper topped iron ore earnings on AI-driven demand [[n5186]].
Reported

BlueScope beat profit estimates and lifted its outlook, yet its shares fell [[n1998]] — steel is not getting the AI-metals multiple. Freeport is up 4.80% over 20 sessions and Newmont 10.15% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
EPS Upside Watch

Copper producers with growth volumes, where earnings mix is shifting from iron ore and coal to the AI and grid metal. FCX and the diversified majors with rising copper share are the cleanest exposure.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Global exchange copper stocks topped 1 million tonnes for the first time in 21 years [[n5189]], while copper at 5.79 is down 2.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Inventories say the price is ahead of physical tightness — own miners' earnings mix, not the metal.
Narrative
XLRE last closed at 43.50, up 4.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), riding the 18 bps five-observation drop in the 10Y to 4.04% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13).
Reported

No major REIT print moved the group in the window; the deal flow spoke instead: Sumitomo Forestry agreed to acquire US homebuilder Tri Pointe Homes in an all-cash deal [[n5152]] — foreign strategic buyers are paying for US housing exposure while domestic transactions stall.
EPS Upside Watch
Data-centre and net-lease landlords benefit from lower yields; homebuilders gain from the Fed's plan to loosen mortgage-lending rules [[n6686]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

HousingWire shows how cheaper rates can make homes less affordable as prices respond [[n6058]] — rate relief is capitalised into prices rather than volumes. Prefer landlords with contracted rents over transaction-driven real estate.
Narrative

XLU last closed at 46.50, up 7.27% over five sessions and 6.63% over 20, with NextEra up 14.13% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Duke's $103B plan, the largest of any regulated US utility [[n1920]], anchors the rate-base growth story.
Reported
Capex plans keep rising through the reporting window, and the market is paying for them. Vistra is up 14.59% over five sessions and Constellation 10.33% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
EPS Upside Watch
Regulated utilities with approved transmission and generation plans carry the most visible EPS growth; merchant generators carry the most leverage to data-centre demand.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Local resistance is rising: a proposal for an 800-acre data center in central Pennsylvania was denied [[n5142]]. Load forecasts are now a political variable — prefer regulated rate bases with approved plans over merchant exposure that depends on every project getting built.
Narrative

The SXAP tracker slipped 0.44% to 46.11 and is up 3.2% over 20 sessions; Volkswagen fell 0.78% and Renault 1.52% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). The sector is restructuring in public, which rarely ends with an immediate re-rating.
Reported

Volkswagen plans to cut costs by 20% by the end of 2028, Manager Magazin reports [[n5111]], and Stellantis will announce full-year 2025 results on February 26 [[n5125]]. Restructuring, not demand, is the sector's earnings driver.
EPS Upside Watch
BMW, up 4.44% over 20 sessions, and Mercedes, flat at 57.65 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16), have the most pricing power; cost programmes protect margins but not volumes.
⚡ Breaking Convention

A 20% cost cut at Europe's largest carmaker [[n5111]] is bullish for its margins and bearish for European suppliers, whose revenue is someone else's cost. Short the supply chain, not the OEMs, if you want the restructuring trade.
Narrative

SOXX last closed at 354.66, up 5.17% over 20 sessions, with Micron up 22.29% and TSMC up 7.24% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The split is widening — AMAT and TSMC gain while Nvidia and Intel retreat [[n5072]] — as the market pays for bottlenecks.
Reported

Applied Materials jumped 8% after a Q1 beat and strong Q2 outlook [[n1999]], confirming equipment demand follows memory pricing. ASML last closed at 1,406.61, up 5.63% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
EPS Upside Watch
TSMC is considering an additional $100 billion investment into Arizona fabs [[n5070]], a direct order pipeline for equipment makers and a tariff hedge for its US customers.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Nvidia is the laggard inside a winning sector, down 2.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), while Intel also retreats [[n5072]]. The market pays the bottlenecks (memory, tools, foundry), not the platforms — own suppliers, avoid device assemblers squeezed by memory costs.

earnings_pattern.title: Beats are table stakes; the market pays for copper, chips and balance sheets
parts: Rewarded

BHP beat as copper overtook iron ore in its earnings [[n5186]], Applied Materials jumped 8% on a beat and strong outlook [[n1999]], and Coinbase rallied 16% after an earnings miss because its balance sheet reassured investors [[n2001]].
Punished

BlueScope beat and lifted its outlook yet fell [[n1998]]; Pinterest sank nearly 17% as tariffs hit earnings [[n1980]]; Cisco dropped 7% despite topping estimates [[n1770]]. Quality of the story beats quality of the quarter.
Pattern

Reuters sums it up for Europe: earnings are gaining pace while lofty valuations cap the rewards [[n2281]]. The market pays for exposure to AI bottlenecks (copper, memory, equipment) and for balance-sheet strength in a downturn, and it fines everything else that merely beats. Over 20 sessions, Micron's 22.29% and Caterpillar's 19.63% 20-session gains contrast with Microsoft's 12.12% fall (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Attention into EPS

Walmart and fresh economic data lead the week ahead [[n0305]], and Stellantis reports full-year results on February 26 [[n5125]]. In Australia, reporting season continues after BHP's beat [[n5186]] — the first large sample of how a strong AUD and a higher cash rate hit guidance.
Playbook

Buy companies whose results show rising exposure to copper, memory, power and equipment; fade beats in sectors where valuation already prices perfection. Watch Walmart's reaction first: a sell-on-beat would confirm that the market is now punishing crowded defensives too, and that the next rotation runs toward oversold growth.

underowned.title: Quality software after the AI wipeout
parts: Attention Gap

Forbes counts $300 billion wiped off software stocks by the brutal pace of AI [[n5085]], and a fund beating 99% of peers sees few survivors [[n5083]] — sentiment is near maximum pessimism, which is when dispersion inside a sector is widest and stock-picking pays.
Exposure & Risk

Build positions in stages in software with proprietary data, high switching costs and clear AI monetisation — Microsoft at 401.32, down 12.12% over 20 sessions, and Oracle at 160.14, down 15.65% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), or the IGV ETF. Risk: seat-based revenue erodes faster than AI revenue arrives; size small until a software beat is rewarded.

underowned.title: Japanese government bonds after the twist-steepening
parts: Attention Gap

Jupiter's Nash has turned into a Japan bond convert after Takaichi's win [[n3148]], following a twist-steepening of the curve on fiscal concerns and the BOJ outlook [[n3094]]. JGBs have long been treated as a funding market rather than an asset; a hawkish BOJ plus a stronger yen is the combination that makes them work for foreign buyers.
Exposure & Risk

Express through yen-denominated intermediate JGBs or JGB futures, keeping the currency open: USD/JPY is down 3.02% over 20 sessions to 152.78 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). Risk: fiscal expansion after the election win pushes long yields higher, and an April hike hits the front end first — prefer the belly over the long end.

crypto.title: Holding the lows, losing the institutions
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 68,843.16, up 0.08% on the day and 2.76% over five sessions but down 22.74% over 20; ether closed at 1,997.92 (up 1.62%, down 33.89% over 20 sessions) and Solana at 86.43 (up 9.05% over five sessions, down 31.98% over 20) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). Bloomberg describes bitcoin looking for direction after four straight weekly losses [[n1223]].
New / Most Important

Institutional allocation is shifting inside crypto: Harvard trimmed its bitcoin ETF holdings by 21% and built an $87 million ether position [[n1230]]. Strategy plans to swap $6B of convertible debt for equity [[n1249]] and says it can survive a bitcoin crash to $8,000 [[n1250]] — balance-sheet repair that dilutes shareholders but lowers forced-selling risk.
Playbook

Stay neutral on bitcoin until it reclaims $70,000 [[n1191]]; the 20-session reference of 89,102.57 shows how much overhead supply remains (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). Prefer ether over Solana for any rebound trade given the institutional rotation, and underweight MSTR as the convertible swap adds equity supply.

flows.title: Dollar safe-haven doubts, Asia inflows, tight credit
parts: Rates & Dollar

DXY last closed at 96.88, down 2.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), and EUR/USD held at 1.1867 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). Deutsche Bank warns that AI risks in US equities are undermining the dollar's safe-haven status [[n6730]] — a regime where US equity drawdowns weaken rather than strengthen the dollar.
Credit Check

HYG closed at 80.85 and LQD at 111.59, with TLT up 2.49% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13): credit is calm and duration is bid. The supply overhang from AI capex remains the medium-term risk, but nothing in spreads signals stress yet.
Portfolio Implication

Follow the flow into Asia: hedge funds bought the most Asian stocks in a decade [[n2579]]. Keep US duration, own non-US equities unhedged to collect the dollar decline, and hold credit at benchmark. Revisit if the dollar rallies on an equity sell-off — that would restore the old safe-haven pattern and argue for re-hedging currency exposure.

anticipatory.title: Geneva: Iran and Ukraine talks on the same day
parts: What Is Priced

Separate Iran and Ukraine-Russia talks are set for Tuesday in Geneva, according to a source [[n2783]]. Oil rose on the US-Iran talks [[n6705]], while Brent at 67.75 is up only 6.26% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13); the US military, meanwhile, is preparing for potentially weeks-long Iran operations [[n2801]].
Conditional Expression

If the Iran track stalls: Brent call spreads, XLE and gold; if it yields a framework, fade the energy premium, with XLE's 14.16% 20-session gain the unwind candidate (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). On Ukraine, progress favours PLN, Polish banks and European cyclicals; a breakdown favours European defence and EUR/PLN calls.
Risk
The Kremlin says territory is on the agenda [[n2820]], the hardest issue, so a headline deal may lack substance and reverse within days. Keep both legs in options and size for gap risk.

anticipatory.title: Fed minutes, GDP and PCE: does the cut repricing survive?
parts: What Is Priced

Traders put 50% odds on three cuts this year [[n6495]], and the market awaits the Fed minutes and US GDP [[n6731]] alongside PCE [[n6703]]. The 2Y at 3.40% sits 16 bps below its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13).
Conditional Expression

Dovish minutes and soft PCE: add 5Y duration, small caps (IWM at 262.96) and gold (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Hawkish minutes or hot PCE: the 2Y back toward 3.56%, a dollar bounce from 96.88, and pressure on rate-sensitive leaders such as XLU and XLRE (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13; Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Risk

The minutes describe a committee before the latest CPI, so they may sound more hawkish than current pricing; and with the chair handover pending, markets may discount the minutes entirely. Avoid outright duration size into the release; use options.

catalysts.title: $WMT — the week's test of the defensive rotation
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Walmart's results lead the week ahead [[n0305]]. The thesis is share gain from both ends of the income distribution; Dollar Tree adding higher-priced items [[n2589]] shows discounters chasing the same trading-down shopper, so the print must prove Walmart is still winning that fight.
Price Hurdle & Risk

WMT last closed at 133.89, up 12.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Use a call spread rather than stock; the risk is SNAP-related basket friction [[n5156]] in the guide, and a sell-on-beat would mean the rotation is spent.

catalysts.title: $MSTR — the convertible swap adds equity supply
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Strategy plans to swap $6B of convertible debt for equity [[n1249]] and says it can survive a bitcoin crash to $8,000 [[n1250]]. Solvency risk falls, but the swap converts debt holders into potential sellers of the stock, capping MSTR's premium to its bitcoin.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MSTR last closed at 133.88, up 8.85% on Friday but down 21.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Prefer short MSTR against long IBIT; the risk is a sharp bitcoin squeeze that lifts the leveraged equity first.

retail.title: Hims & Hers / HIMS — the crowded-short dip-buy
parts: Observed Attention
24/7 Wall St. highlights 84% analyst upside in Hims & Hers despite this month's 48% sell-off [[n3891]], while hedge funds bet big against the stock before a Wegovy showdown [[n2519]].
Motivation & Bias
Anchoring on old highs and price targets, plus the hope of a short squeeze. Retail is treating a 48% drop as a discount; the shorts are treating it as a business-model question.
Instrument & Risk
If you play it, use defined-risk call spreads sized for a total loss; generic semaglutide and branded price competition can compress the cash-pay model regardless of the squeeze.

retail.title: Qualcomm / QCOM — Reddit sentiment capitulates
parts: Observed Attention
Qualcomm hit oversold territory as Reddit sentiment crashed below 30 [[n2016]] — retail is giving up on a handset-chip name in the middle of a memory squeeze.
Motivation & Bias

Recency bias: the AI-fuelled chip shortage is driving up smartphone prices [[n4941]], and retail extrapolates that into lost units for chip suppliers. Washed-out sentiment on a cash-generative name is often a contrarian signal.
Instrument & Risk
Contrarians can scale in with small position sizes; the risk is that device makers cut builds as memory costs rise, hitting modem and application-processor volumes for several quarters.

retail.title: Reddit / RDDT — insiders buy the 46% drop
parts: Observed Attention
An insider sent a major vote of confidence after earnings [[n3881]], after the stock declined 46% in a month [[n3821]]. Retail followers track insider buying as a bottom signal.
Motivation & Bias
Authority bias — following insiders — mixed with the narrative that Reddit's data is valuable to AI training. Insider buying is a necessary but not sufficient signal; timing can be months early.
Instrument & Risk
Use the stock rather than options, given volatility premiums after a crash. The risk is ad-revenue sensitivity in a softer ad market, as Pinterest's reaction showed.

retail.title: Silver coins & SLV — physical buyers meet the dealers
parts: Observed Attention
Near-record gold and silver prices have coin and jewelry exchange shops busy [[n5203]]. SLV last closed at 69.72, down 16.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Motivation & Bias
Two retail crowds at once: sellers cashing in at high prices and dip-buyers chasing the debasement story. That two-way physical flow adds supply into rallies.
Instrument & Risk
Prefer GLD, up 9.28% over 20 sessions, to SLV for metals exposure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13); silver's 15% 20-session drawdown shows its higher beta cuts both ways.
